newsitem.title: UK: BA says keeping cargo flying despite strike threat.
newsitem.headline: BA says keeping cargo flying despite strike threat.

text.p: British Airways World Cargo said Thursday it plans to "keep flying" and "offer our cargo customers the services they rely on" after a cabin crew vote for strike action.
"We have contingency plans ready to put in place," said a BA cargo spokesman, without giving further details.

On Wednesday, the Transport and General Workers Union (T&G) said an overwhelming majority of cabin crew had voted for a strike after a bitter five-month-long pay row and it would decide its next move on Monday.

While the majority of BA's cargo is flown in the bellyholds of passenger aircraft, the carrier also leases pure freighter aircraft for certain key ex-London cargo routes -- for example, to Hong Kong, Johannesburg and, from this autumn, Israel.

Market analysts said that to continue offering freight customers an acceptable service during a strike, BA World Cargo would have to increase its all-cargo flights, which should be unaffected by T&G cabin crew union action, and also buy cargo space from other airlines.

They added that the possible strike action would come at a bad time for BA World Cargo, which is anxious to improve on its financial performance for the year-ended March 31, when its revenues fell by one million stg compared to a year earlier, to 565 million stg.
This was blamed on increased capacity in the marketplace accompanied by fierce competition.
BA's cargo volume, however, rose eight percent in 1996-97 to 721,146 tonnes.
-Bob Murphy, Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel,+44 171 542 7706; Fax +5017
